newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila mid-caps to outshine blue chips - broker.
newsitem.headline: Manila mid-caps to outshine blue chips - broker.

text.p: Manila brokerage firm Sun Hung Kai Securities (Phil) Inc on Monday recommended six mid-sized companies, saying the firms would likely outperform large-capitalisation issues.
"These are the emerging blue chips which should outperform existing blue chips within nine months to a year," said Sun Hung Kai vice-president Raul Ruiz in a presentation.

Ruiz said the companies which should be bought due to their attractive valuations are Asian Terminals Inc, Fortune Cement Corp, Interphil Laboratories Inc, Mabuhay Vinyl Corp, PCI Leasing & Finance Corp and RFM Corp.
Despite the bullish performance of the stock market at the beginning of this year, Sun Hung Kai said political issues will continue to impinge on the market, particularly on blue chips.
"Aside from being less vulnerable to these systemic risks, our more important argument for investing in select mid-sized stocks is of course valuation," said Sun Hung Kai.

Sun Hung Kai data showed the projected annual growth in earnings per share (EPS) in 1997 of its six favoured stocks ranged from -12.5 to 154.8 percent as against six blue chips with an estimated EPS ranging from 13.7 to 33.0 percent this year.
The projected EPS decline of 12.5 percent is for Mabuhay Vinyl, which is expected to make a turnaround next year, the broker said.
Blue chips used in the comparison were PLDT, San Miguel Corp, Manila Electric Co, Ayala Corp, Metrobank & Trust Co and Petron Corp.
